Based on your search terms, you seem to be mixing real-world concepts with custom, adult-oriented (NSFW) modifications for Fallout 4. 
1. "Lewdie Mag 4" & "Cryptic Valentine"
In the vanilla game, there is no item called a "Lewdie Mag." However, the Fallout 4 adult modding community (found on platforms like Nexus Mods or LoversLab) frequently creates custom retextures for in-game skill magazines. 
  • The Base Quest: "Cryptic Valentine" is likely a reference to the prominent early-game main quest "Unlikely Valentine", where you rescue the synth private eye, Nick Valentine, from Vault 114. 
  • The Magazine: During this specific quest inside Vault 114, you can find a real vanilla magazine: Astoundingly Awesome Tales #8. If you have an adult texture pack or a custom item mod installed (often colloquially called "lewdie" or adult magazine mods), it will replace or add custom collectible magazines in these quest areas. 
2. "Erica Synth"
This term points to one of two possibilities: 
  • Real-World Tech: Erica Synths is a very famous, real-world manufacturer of modular Eurorack synthesizers and audio equipment. It has no official connection to Fallout 4. 
  • Custom Companion Mod: If you are looking for an in-game synth character named Erica, it is a custom NPC added via a third-party mod. The closest highly-rated lore companion mod is Synthetic Love, which adds a voiced female Gen-3 synth companion. 
Summary: If you are trying to find a specific collectible magazine from an adult mod pack during Nick Valentine's rescue quest, check the room where you fight Dino or the living quarters of Vault 114 where Astoundingly Awesome Tales naturally spawns!
